steps.name: TMM normalization and 20-gene signature scoring
caveats: The record does not state whether Salmon length correction was applied; for a fixed 20-gene panel this does not materially affect cross-sample score comparison, but state it in the report
If the values look like TPM/FPKM rather than counts, say so and justify the normalization choice before proceeding
A median score can diverge from the mean score when individual signature genes are extreme in some samples; report both so the downstream step can use the mean as primary
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-survival-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 120 samples; the record does not state whether length correction was applied); /eval-four-models-v2-without-survival-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (120 x 4: sample, condition case/control, follow-up time, event); /eval-four-models-v2-without-survival-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/signature/signature_genes.csv (20 gene symbols, one per row, no weights). Design: 60 cases vs. 60 controls, unpaired, single batch. R is available with edgeR 4.10.3 and ggplot2 4.0.3.
steps.question: What is each of the 120 tumor-biopsy samples' level of the pre-specified 20-gene signature (unweighted), on a scale comparable across the case and control samples?
constraints: Score all 120 samples; no sample exclusion at this step
If a signature symbol is absent from the count matrix, score on the remaining genes and flag it prominently in the output — never impute
Save the per-sample score table as a CSV artifact in the step output directory
steps.description: Load counts.csv and metadata.csv; join on sample id and verify exactly 120/120 match, reporting any mismatch. Map the 20 signature symbols to count rows and report the exact matched/unmatched list. Sanity-check that values look like raw counts (non-negative, integer-like). TMM-normalize the full 12000x120 matrix with edgeR (calcNormFactors + cpm) and compute, per sample, the unweighted mean of the 20 signature genes' normalized expression as the primary score, plus the unweighted median as a robustness variant. QC: per-sample total counts and detected-gene counts; flag low-count or outlier samples (flag only, do not drop). Write a per-sample CSV (sample, condition, score_mean, score_median, norm_factor, QC flags) and a brief distribution summary/plot of the scores by condition.
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample score table (CSV) covering all 120 samples with condition carried through, containing both mean- and median-based scores
Explicit report of how many of the 20 signature symbols matched the count rows, naming any unmatched
TMM normalization factors reported and raw-count sanity check documented
QC flags (not drops) for any low-count or outlier samples, with the flagged sample list

steps.name: Cox PH: time-to-event ~ signature score + condition
caveats: Median-score split KM is descriptive and does not adjust for condition; do not present it as a test of the adjusted association
If condition is strongly associated with the event, the adjusted HR for score reflects association partly within strata; the within-case sensitivity makes the single-stratum view visible
The signature is pre-specified by the study and not derived from this cohort's data, so the test is not inflated by in-sample feature selection — state this as an assumption of the analysis
Censoring is assumed non-informative; no competing risks are modeled (single binary event indicator)
steps.context: Uses T1S1's per-sample table (score_mean, score_median, condition) joined to metadata.csv columns: time (follow-up) and event (0/1 indicator). Validate before modeling: time >= 0, event in {0,1}, and 0 < event rate < 100%; if the event column is degenerate (all 0 or all 1), stop and report — a Cox model is undefined. Python environment has lifelines 0.30.0; R's survival package is NOT installed, so all survival modeling must run in Python with lifelines.
steps.question: In the full 120-sample cohort (60 cases vs. 60 controls), does the 20-gene signature score associate with time to the event after accounting for case versus control status, and is that association stable under PH diagnostics and within-case sensitivity?
constraints: Fit the primary model with BOTH score and condition; never drop the condition covariate from the primary analysis
Use the mean-based score as the primary predictor; the median-based score is sensitivity only
Count and report events before interpreting any p-value
Run survival modeling in Python with lifelines (R survival package is not installed)
steps.description: Report total events overall and per condition before any inference, and state explicitly whether the cohort is underpowered (rule-of-thumb events per covariate) if few. Primary model: Cox PH event(time) ~ score_z + condition with score_z = T1S1 mean-based score standardized to 1-SD units; report HR per 1-SD of score with 95% CI and Wald p-value, plus the unadjusted score-only model for reference. PH assumption: Schoenfeld residual tests (overall and per covariate); if violated for score, additionally fit a time-varying effect (product with log time) and a model restricted to the early follow-up window, and interpret in light of the violation. Descriptive: Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank p-values for median-score split (high vs. low) and for condition, labeled as unadjusted. Sensitivity: Cox restricted to the 60 cases, with its own event count; median-based score as an alternate predictor in the primary model. State explicitly that this is a prognostic (not predictive) association because the metadata carries no treatment variable.
acceptance_criteria: Condition-adjusted Cox result: HR per 1-SD of signature score with 95% CI and p-value, alongside the unadjusted score-only model
Event counts (overall and per condition) reported before interpretation, with an explicit power statement
Schoenfeld PH test results, with a documented response (time-varying effect and/or early-window model) if the assumption is violated
Kaplan-Meier curves plus log-rank p-values for median score split and for condition, explicitly labeled unadjusted
Within-cases-only sensitivity result with its event count
Explicit statement that the test is prognostic, not predictive, and that the signature is pre-specified rather than derived on this cohort

plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs. time-to-event, case-adjusted
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 60 cases vs. 60 controls of unpaired human tumor biopsies: Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 120 samples), per-sample follow-up time and 0/1 event indicator, and a pre-specified, unweighted 20-gene signature (symbols only, no weights). The research question is a prognostic association test of a pre-specified signature, not model discovery. Step 1 reduces the matrix to one comparable per-sample score: edgeR TMM normalization over the full 12000x120 matrix (the record's unknown Salmon length-correction status does not materially affect a fixed 20-gene panel, and will be stated as such), then the unweighted mean (plus median robustness variant) of the 20 signature genes per sample, with symbol-mapping and sample-level QC reported rather than silently fixed. Step 2 tests the question: Cox proportional hazards with event(time) ~ score + condition on the full 120-sample cohort — condition is a required covariate per the question, so the primary result is the condition-adjusted HR per 1-SD of score — with event-count/power checks upfront, Schoenfeld PH diagnostics and a documented response if violated, descriptive Kaplan-Meier by median score split and by condition, and a within-cases-only sensitivity. R's survival package is absent from the sandbox, so the modeling runs in Python with lifelines.
